skill.name: using-git-worktrees
skill.description: Use Git worktrees to create isolated development workspaces without disturbing the current working tree.
skill.summary: Git worktree workflow for isolated development branches.
skill.author: CodingCossack

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown formatting or normal local Git workflow examples, not Ruby backtick execution or suspicious hidden-file access. The skill still directs agents to run dependency setup and create commits automatically, which can execute project code or alter repository history without explicit user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Automatic dependency setup can execute project-defined code.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for user confirmation before running install, build, download, or test commands in untrusted repositories.
Show the .gitignore diff and ask before creating a commit or changing branch history.

remediation.issue: The global hidden worktree path may surprise users.
remediation.suggestion: Make the home-directory location explicitly opt-in and report the resolved absolute path before use.

static_findings.snippet: **If found:** Use that directory. If both exist, `.worktrees` wins.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Dependency Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to automatically run project setup commands such as package installs, builds, and module downloads. These commands can execute project-defined scripts or download dependencies before user review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 101-118 explicitly direct automatic setup for Node.js, Rust, Python, and Go projects. Package installation and build commands commonly execute local or third-party code.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Repository Commit
semantic_findings.description: The workflow tells the agent to add a missing worktree ignore rule and commit the change immediately. Creating commits without explicit confirmation can alter repository history and include unintended local edits.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly require adding a .gitignore entry and committing it when the pattern is absent. This is a clear source-control integrity concern, even though it appears operational rather than malicious.

content.value_statement: Parallel development can disturb the current branch and hide baseline failures. This skill guides directory selection, ignore checks, setup commands, and baseline tests for Git worktrees.
actual_capabilities: Selects an existing .worktrees or worktrees directory using a defined priority.
Checks CLAUDE.md for worktree directory preferences before asking the user.
Verifies project-local worktree directories are listed in .gitignore.
Creates a new Git worktree and branch with the selected path.
Detects common project files and runs matching setup commands.
Runs baseline tests and reports the final worktree location.
limitations: Requires a Git repository with Git worktree support.
May run package installation or test commands from project configuration.
Does not define cleanup steps after the branch is finished.
Assumes the agent can use shell commands in the local workspace.

use_cases.title: Feature Branch Isolation
use_cases.description: Create a separate workspace before implementing a feature so the current branch remains unchanged.

use_cases.title: Baseline Test Verification
use_cases.description: Run setup and tests in a fresh worktree before starting risky changes.

use_cases.title: Parallel Agent Work
use_cases.description: Give an AI coding agent a separate branch and directory for implementation work.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Worktree
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe Git worktree for this feature. Follow the skill workflow, verify directory rules, and report the final path before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Respect Project Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up a Git worktree for this issue. Check existing worktree folders and CLAUDE.md preferences before choosing a location.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Clean Baseline
prompt_templates.scenario: Confirm the new workspace is ready.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a worktree for this branch, run the appropriate project setup, run baseline tests, and summarize any failures before continuing.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Parallel Development
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an isolated worktree for this implementation plan, preserve the current branch, verify ignore rules, and report setup, tests, and next steps.

output_examples.input: Create a worktree for an authentication feature.
output: Selected the existing project-local worktree directory.
Confirmed the directory is ignored by Git.
Created a new branch workspace and completed baseline checks.

output_examples.input: Prepare an isolated workspace for a bug fix.
output_examples.output: The report identifies the chosen worktree location, setup commands run, test status, and whether implementation can proceed.

output_examples.input: Set up parallel agent work without changing my current branch.
output_examples.output: The agent creates a separate worktree, enters that workspace, and reports the path before starting the requested changes.

best_practices: Confirm the selected worktree directory matches repository conventions before creating branches.
Review .gitignore changes before committing them to the repository.
Run baseline tests before implementation so existing failures are visible.
anti_patterns: Creating a project-local worktree before checking .gitignore.
Running setup commands in an untrusted repository without user confirmation.
Continuing after failed baseline tests without reporting the failures.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps agents create separate Git workspaces so development can continue without disturbing the current branch.

faq.question: Does it require Git worktree support?
faq.answer: Yes. The repository must be a Git repository that supports worktrees.

faq.question: Will it choose a directory automatically?
faq.answer: It first checks existing worktree directories, then CLAUDE.md preferences, then asks the user if no preference exists.

faq.question: Why does it check .gitignore?
faq.answer: Project-local worktrees should be ignored so nested workspace files are not accidentally added to the repository.

faq.question: Can it run project setup commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It can detect common project files and run matching setup commands, depending on local permissions.

faq.question: Does it clean up worktrees after use?
faq.answer: No. Cleanup is listed as a paired workflow and is not defined inside this skill.
